title: NASA Unveils $10 Billion Plan for a Moon Base by 2032
summary:
NASA has big plans for the Moon. On Saturday, November 7, the space agency announced up to $10 billion in new contracts to help build a permanent moon base for astronauts by 2032.

The biggest piece is a new framework called CLPS 2, short for Commercial Lunar Payload Services. It is worth up to $10 billion over ten years. NASA picked eight companies to compete for missions under it: Blue Origin, Firefly Aerospace, Intuitive Machines, ispace-U.S., Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, SpaceX and Voyager Technologies. NASA also raised the ceiling of its existing CLPS contract from $2.6 billion to $4.2 billion.

Why the change? NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said the old contract was all or nothing, which worked for one or two missions a year. Scaling up needs flexibility to move pieces around, he said.

The plan also includes a nuclear-powered robot rover called PROMISE, short for Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration. It will explore the Moon's south pole starting in late 2028, carrying a drill and science instruments to search for water ice and other volatiles. NASA gave Blue Origin a $94 million contract, with a possible $140 million more based on performance, to deliver PROMISE aboard its Blue Moon Mark 1 lander.

NASA also awarded about $1.3 billion in launch and transport work to Arrow Science and Technology, Blue Origin and Impulse Space. Those missions will test cargo transfers between Earth and lunar orbits, navigation with the CAPSTONE 2 spacecraft and lunar scouting with MoonFall drones. SpaceX will launch communications satellites aboard Starship in 2028.

All of this supports NASA's Phase One Moon Base strategy, which runs through 2029 and focuses on robots, infrastructure tests and commercial deliveries. Phase Two, from 2029 to 2032, will keep building the base.
why_it_matters: A moon base could become a home and workplace for astronauts far from Earth, and the robots, landers and tests in this plan are the first steps toward living and working on another world.

background_read: NASA is the United States space agency, and it sends astronauts and robots into space.
The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite, and astronauts have never lived there for long stays, so a base would need homes, power and supplies brought from Earth.
Under its CLPS programme, NASA pays private companies to carry science tools and cargo to the Moon instead of building every lander itself.
Water ice at the Moon's south pole matters because it could be turned into drinking water, air and even rocket fuel for future trips.
